# JIT 403 + long-poll

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P3 · Act as the user](../README.md#phase-3--act-as-the-user) · **Lane:** Worker · **Label:** `feature:jit-authorization` · **Epic:** [#144](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/144) · **Tickets:** 7 (2S 5M)

When a per-user placeholder cannot be resolved because the user has no grant, the worker does not forward the request. It asks the CP to create or reuse a pending authorization and answers with a structured authorization_required response: a 403 JSON body for HTTP, a JSON-RPC result or error for MCP, and grpc-status 7 for gRPC. The CP owns the authorize and status URLs, derives the scopes from policy, and serves a status long-poll that wakes within a second of consent. Deployments without perUser mappings never enter this path.

## How we build it

- Scope and opt-in: the JIT stage runs only when W-P3-PUS-04 sets s.authRequired because the worker UserTokenSource (W-P3-PUS-09) got grant_missing, scope_insufficient or reconsent_required from the CP mint (W-P3-PUS-07). Deployments without perUser mappings never enter the stage and behave byte-identically. Requests from users who already hold a grant pay no JIT cost.
- Error split, always fail-closed: A grant error gives 403 authorization_required. user_token_unavailable (CP, grant store or provider refresh down) stays the W-P3-PUS-04 503 {error:"user_token_unavailable"} with Retry-After and creates no pending. CP unreachable, 4xx/5xx, 429 or the breaker open gives 503 {error:"authorization_unavailable"} with Retry-After. No path forwards the request or sends any part of it upstream.
- Shared wire types: new leaf package internal/connect (no CP, SQLite or oauthbroker imports) holds AuthorizationRequired, PendingRequest/PendingResponse, the Status enum (pending|granted|denied|expired) and the HTTP, JSON-RPC and gRPC response builders. internal/proxy uses it now; internal/mcp/stdio and the P4 MCP gateway (W-P4-MGW-07) can use it later.
- HTTP body (403, Content-Type application/json, Cache-Control no-store), written by a new writeJSONResponse helper beside writeErrorResponse in internal/proxy/http.go: {error:"authorization_required", version:1, kind:"oauth_connect", reason:"grant_missing"|"scope_insufficient"|"reconsent_required", provider, scopes, pending_id, authorize_url, status_url, status_token, expires_at, expires_in, message}. It never carries sub, email, an access token or the upstream URL, and never uses 401 or WWW-Authenticate (same rule as W-P2-WBND-03). Keep-alive is kept when the request body was fully read; otherwise Connection: close.
- The CP owns all URLs and text. authorize_url = <consent.publicURL>/portal/connect/<pending_id> (the W-P3-PORT-03 landing page) and status_url = <consent.publicURL>/connect/<pending_id>/status. consent.publicURL is a new CP-local key in the W-P3-CSIG-01 consent block: absolute https (http only for loopback), defaulting to the origin of consent.oidc.redirectURL, never on the policy wire. The worker copies URLs from the CP response unchanged. message comes from a fixed CP template built from the agent id, provider display name and scopes; nothing supplied by the agent or upstream is stored or shown on the portal.
- Worker to CP: POST /control/connect/pending {subject_token, placeholder, reason, request:{method, host, path, mcp_tool}} on the single cert-presenting CP client from W-P2-WCA-03, listed in the W-P1-SSO-05 authz route table. Like POST /control/user-token (W-P3-PUS-07), it accepts only a worker cert principal (W-P2-WCA-04) and re-verifies the user's Warden token on the CP with the same verifier, so idp_iss, sub and the agent (act.sub, which must equal the worker's heartbeat agentID from W-P2-AREG-05, stored by W-P2-AREG-03; else 403 agent_mismatch) come from the token, never from the worker. user_key = secrets.UserKey(idp_iss, sub). The CP derives the provider and scopes = mapping.scopes ∩ provider.AllowedScopes from the perUserSecrets mapping (W-P3-PUS-02) with the W-P3-BRKR-01 CapScopes helper; the worker never sends sub, agent or scopes. An unknown placeholder or an agent not in the mapping gets 409. Limits (internal/ratelimit from W-P3-BRKR-03): 60/min per worker principal and 20 active pendings per user_key, else 429. With /control/user-token this is one of two accepted new worker→CP calls, used only after a grant error; both are worker-cert (mTLS) only, rate-limited and re-verify the user token on the CP, and docs/architecture.md and docs/control-plane.md list them (W-P3-JIT-01).
- CP create-or-reuse in internal/oauthbroker on top of the W-P3-BRKR-02 GrantStore: if an active grant already covers the scopes, return {status:"granted"} and the worker re-runs swapSecrets once. Otherwise return the active pending for (user_key, agent_id, provider, scopes_key), backed by a partial unique index WHERE status='pending' with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and a re-read, or create one: 128-bit random id, consent.connect.pendingTTL (W-P3-BRKR-01, default 15m), origin jit, created_by_proxy_id, reason and request metadata (method, host, path without query, MCP tool) in the W-P3-BRKR-02 request columns, which the W-P3-PORT-03 landing page shows. status_token = base64url(HMAC-SHA256(CP-local key, pending_id)), so a reused pending returns the same token and nothing is stored.
- MCP over HTTP: the stage classifies the request itself, using s.wasMCP when set and otherwise protocol.IsMCP on the cached s.reqBody (mcpRequestScan returns early when s.gw is nil). tools/call with an id gets HTTP 200 with JSON-RPC result {isError:true, content:[{type:"text", text: message + authorize_url}], structuredContent: <body>} and the request id echoed verbatim. Other methods with an id get JSON-RPC error -32042 (MCP URL-elicitation-required) with data {elicitations:[{mode:"url", elicitationId: pending_id, url: authorize_url, message}], warden: <body>}. Notifications, batches and legacy HTTP+SSE POSTs get the HTTP 403 JSON. The reply is application/json unless Accept excludes it, in which case one SSE message event is sent. This JSON-RPC answer is a documented exception to the W-P2-WBND-03 rule that MCP denies stay plain JSON. stdio is out of scope: internal/mcp/stdio does no secret swap, and a stdio server's own egress gets the HTTP 403.
- h2 and gRPC: serveGRPCStream in internal/proxy/grpc.go swaps outside runRequestStages, so the same JIT logic runs there. Non-gRPC h2 streams get the 403 JSON; application/grpc gets grpc-status 7 (PERMISSION_DENIED) with grpc-message 'authorization_required <authorize_url>'. Neither forwards anything.
- Worker cost and resilience: CP calls time out after 3s and are de-duplicated with singleflight per (user_key, agent, provider). A bounded LRU (10,000 entries) caches the pending response until min(expires_at − 30s, 5m) and drops entries when userGrantEpochs[user_key] changes. After a CP failure a per-key breaker fails fast for 5s. The UserTokenSource lookup (W-P3-PUS-09, which never caches grant errors) still runs on every request, so a retry right after consent succeeds.
- Status: GET /connect/{id}/status?wait=Ns, clamped with parseWait (moved from internal/controlplane/policyserver.go to new internal/longpoll so oauthbroker can use it) to 1–60s, returns {status, reason, expires_at, expires_in} with Cache-Control no-store. Accepted credentials: Authorization: Bearer <status_token> (constant-time compare; never in the URL because the worker records Event.URL), a worker credential whose heartbeat agentID equals the pending's agent_id (the P4 park waiter path), or a portal session (W-P3-CSIG-04) whose (iss, sub) matches the pending. Unknown ids and wrong credentials all get the same 404. The handler re-reads the row on entry, on every wake, every 5s and on timeout, and reports expires_at <= now as expired without waiting for the retention ticker.
- Waking: waiters wait on the W-P3-BRKR-02 GrantStore Subscribe channel, which closes on CompletePending and on expiry, so the BRKR-04 callback and the PORT-03 decline call sites do not change. A thin decorator adds one rule: CompletePending(granted) also marks every active pending for the same (user_key, provider) whose scopes are a subset of the granted scopes as granted and closes their channels. Waiters are bounded at 2,048 global and 8 per pending (429 Retry-After: 1 beyond that); a map entry is removed when its last waiter leaves.
- Degraded modes: CP down gives 503 authorization_unavailable while requests that already hold a grant keep working. IdP down means portal login fails and the pending stays pending until expiry. Clients use expires_in, so clock skew does not matter. A worker restart loses only its cache; the CP de-duplicates. A CP restart drops in-flight polls and clients re-poll; pendings persist in SQLite. Cross-replica wakeups wait for p5-postgres-ha; the 5s re-read keeps answers correct meanwhile.
- Events and observability: each JIT response stores one deny event through recordEvent (W-P1-VRFY-03) with Reason authorization_required or authorization_unavailable (added to internal/proxy/reasons.go from W-P1-JAUD-06 and to RecordBlocked; user_token_unavailable comes from W-P3-PUS-04), the pre-swap URL from W-P1-JAUD-05, user_sub stamped, and the OAuth provider in Event.UserTokenProvider (W-P3-PUS-10), never Event.Provider (that is the LLM cost provider). bridgeEvent in internal/alertpipeline raises no finding for these reasons. Worker counter warden.jit.total{outcome, provider} with provider limited to configured ids, else other. CP counters for pending and status outcomes, completed_at on pendings, and one info log per state change without sub. No token, status_token or body appears in any log or event.
- Back-compat and rollout: the CP is upgraded first; a worker that gets 404 from an older CP treats it as authorization_unavailable. The authorization_required body is versioned and fields may only be added. Operators must allowlist the consent.publicURL origin for agents that should poll status; JIT never auto-allows it.

## Done when

In a deployment with a CP running consent, the OAuth broker and the portal, an enrolled worker with a cert (W-P2-WCA) and a perUser Google mapping: a request missing a grant gets a 403 authorization_required body matching the golden fixture and docs/schemas/authorization_required.v1.json, the fake upstream receives zero requests, and one deny event with Reason authorization_required is stored. An MCP tools/call over Streamable HTTP gets the isError result with its own request id whether or not the MCP gateway is configured, and an h2 gRPC call gets grpc-status 7. authorize_url opens the portal landing page; after consent, a status long-poll held with the status_token returns granted within 1s on a single-replica CP, and the agent's single retry reaches upstream with that user's token. With the CP stopped the worker returns 503 authorization_unavailable, with the CP refresh path failing it returns 503 user_token_unavailable, and neither forwards the request. A deployment with no perUser mappings behaves byte-identically to before.

### 1/7 · W-P3-JIT-01

**Add CP endpoint to create or reuse pending authorizations**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#145](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/145)

Add POST /control/connect/pending on the CP so a worker can turn a missing grant into a pending authorization the user can approve. The CP authenticates the worker, re-verifies the user's Warden token so the user and agent never come from the worker, derives the scopes from the perUserSecrets mapping, and creates or reuses one pending per (user, agent, provider, scopes). It owns the authorize and status URLs, the user-facing message and the status token, so nothing the agent or worker supplies reaches the portal. This is control-plane only and is mounted only when consent.providers is configured.

**Requirements**

- Route POST /control/connect/pending in internal/oauthbroker, mounted in controlplane.go Handler() only when consent.providers is non-empty (otherwise 404), accepting only a worker cert principal from WorkerAuthenticator (W-P1-WTOK-02, W-P2-WCA-04), like W-P3-PUS-07, and listed as worker-plane in the W-P1-SSO-05 authz route table. wwt_ tokens, user tokens, portal or console sessions and wak_ keys get the uniform 401.
- Request body {subject_token, placeholder, reason, request:{method, host, path, mcp_tool}} is capped at 32 KiB, like W-P3-PUS-07, and decoded with DisallowUnknownFields. The CP verifies subject_token with the W-P3-PUS-07 WardenVerifier and takes idp_iss, sub and act.sub from it; act.sub must equal the worker's heartbeat agentID (W-P2-AREG-05, stored by W-P2-AREG-03), otherwise 403 agent_mismatch; a Dex or invalid token gets 403 identity_required. user_key = secrets.UserKey(idp_iss, sub). reason is grant_missing, scope_insufficient or reconsent_required.
- Scopes are derived, never taken from the worker: the provider and scopes = mapping.scopes ∩ provider.AllowedScopes come from the perUserSecrets mapping for the placeholder, using the W-P3-BRKR-01 CapScopes helper, canonicalized (sorted, de-duplicated) into scopes_key. An unknown placeholder or an agent not listed in the mapping returns 409 and writes no row.
- If an active grant in GrantStore already covers the scopes, return 200 {status:"granted"}. Otherwise return the active pending (status=pending and expires_at > now) for (user_key, agent_id, provider, scopes_key) with 200, or create one with 201: 128-bit random base64url id, TTL consent.connect.pendingTTL (W-P3-BRKR-01), origin jit, created_by_proxy_id from the worker principal, reason, and request metadata (method, host, path without query, MCP tool) in the W-P3-BRKR-02 request columns.
- A migration on pending_authorizations (W-P3-BRKR-02) adds scopes_key, origin, created_by_proxy_id and the JIT reason (completed_at and the request columns already exist), plus a partial unique index on (user_key, agent_id, provider, scopes_key) WHERE status='pending'. Inserts use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING followed by a re-select, so racing workers get one row.
- Response {status, pending_id, authorize_url, status_url, status_token, expires_at, expires_in, message}. URLs are built from new CP-local key consent.publicURL (absolute https, http only for loopback, default the origin of consent.oidc.redirectURL, never on the policy wire). status_token = base64url(HMAC-SHA256(CP-local key, pending_id)) with the key generated on first use and kept in CP SQLite. message comes from a fixed template (agent id, provider display name, scopes). The body never contains sub or email.
- Limits (internal/ratelimit from W-P3-BRKR-03): 60 requests/min per worker principal and 20 active pendings per user_key; over either, 429 with Retry-After. Counter warden_cp_connect_pending_total{outcome=created|reused|already_granted|rejected|rate_limited} and one info log per call with pending_id, proxy_id, agent, provider, scopes_count and outcome; no sub at info level and never the status_token.
- docs/architecture.md and docs/control-plane.md replace the statement that there are exactly three worker→CP calls with the full list: /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest, plus the two P3 calls POST /control/user-token (W-P3-PUS-07, on a worker cache miss) and POST /control/connect/pending (this ticket, deny path only, fail-closed). Both P3 calls require a worker cert (mTLS, W-P2-WCA-04), are rate-limited per worker principal, and the CP re-verifies the user's Warden token on every call.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/config: add consent.publicURL to the W-P3-CSIG-01 consent block with validation, strict-field registration and EncodeNode support; keep it off the policy wire.
2. internal/oauthbroker: new migration for the pending_authorizations columns and partial unique index; add GrantStore.FindActivePending(ctx, userKey, agent, provider, scopesKey) and CreatePendingIfAbsent (both new) and a status key helper (new statuskey.go).
3. New internal/oauthbroker/pending_http.go: handler that validates the body, verifies subject_token with the W-P3-PUS-07 verifier, checks act.sub against the heartbeat agentID, derives scopes from perUserSecrets with the BRKR-01 CapScopes helper, checks GrantStore for a covering grant, and creates or reuses the pending; build URLs, message and status_token.
4. New internal/connect package (leaf, no CP or SQLite imports): PendingRequest, PendingResponse and the Status enum shared with the worker in W-P3-JIT-02.
5. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go Handler(): mount the route behind WorkerAuthenticator when consent is configured, add the authz table row, and add the per-principal and per-user_key limiters.
6. Tests in internal/oauthbroker/pending_http_test.go: dedupe race, auth matrix, agent mismatch, scope derivation, already-granted short circuit, limits, response shape; update docs/architecture.md and docs/control-plane.md.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given 50 goroutines posting the same subject token and placeholder, all receive the same pending_id and exactly one active row exists: `go test -race ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestCreatePendingDedupe`.
- [ ] No credential, a wwt_ token, a portal cookie or a wak_ key gets 401; a worker cert with a valid subject token gets 201, and a Dex ID token as subject_token gets 403 identity_required: `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestPendingAuth`.
- [ ] A subject token whose act.sub differs from the worker's heartbeat agentID gets 403 agent_mismatch, an unknown placeholder gets 409, and sub, agent or scopes in the body are rejected as unknown fields; stored scopes equal mapping scopes ∩ allowedScopes.
- [ ] When a grant covering the scopes exists the response is {status:"granted"} and no row is written; the 21st active pending for one user gets 429.
- [ ] The response contains no sub or email, its status_token verifies for that pending_id and a one-byte change fails: `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestPendingResponseShape`.
- [ ] With consent.providers absent the route returns 404 and `go test ./internal/controlplane` passes unchanged, including TestAuthzRouteCoverage.

### 2/7 · W-P3-JIT-02

**Return structured 403 for HTTP when a grant is missing**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#146](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/146)

Add a jitDeny stage in internal/proxy that runs when W-P3-PUS-04 reports a missing grant. It asks the CP for a pending through a new CreatePending call on the shared cert-presenting CP client and answers 403 authorization_required, or 503 when the CP or secret backend is unavailable; the request is never forwarded. A bounded cache with singleflight keeps agent retries from reaching the CP. This is worker-only and runs only for perUser mappings.

**Requirements**

- New jitDeny stage in runRequestStages right after swapSecrets, entered only when W-P3-PUS-04 set s.authRequired (grant_missing, scope_insufficient or reconsent_required). user_token_unavailable keeps the W-P3-PUS-04 503 and makes no CP call. The stage never calls forward or dialUpstream.
- New RemoteProvider.CreatePending(ctx, connect.PendingRequest) on the W-P2-WCA-03 shared CP client, injected through a new atomic Proxy seam (SetPendingCreator; nil means unavailable), with a 3s timeout and a 16 KiB response limit. It sends the raw Warden token that W-P3-PUS-04 keeps on connIdentity as subject_token, the placeholder name, the reason and the request metadata; never sub, agent or scopes.
- Worker cache: LRU of at most 10,000 entries keyed by (user_key, agent, provider) holding the response until min(expires_at − 30s, 5m), dropped when userGrantEpochs[user_key] changes; singleflight per key; a CP failure opens a 5s per-key breaker. A {status:"granted"} reply makes the stage re-run swapSecrets once and continue normally.
- Success: 403 written by a new writeJSONResponse(w, status, headers, v) helper with Content-Type application/json, Cache-Control: no-store and the internal/connect AuthorizationRequired body (version 1). Connection: close when the request body was not fully read. CP timeout, 4xx, 5xx, 429, open breaker or nil creator give 503 {error:"authorization_unavailable", provider, message} with Retry-After: 5.
- Golden fixtures in internal/proxy/testdata/jit/ and new docs/schemas/authorization_required.v1.json, checked against the internal/connect structs with the W-P1-JAUD-02 struct-tag comparison (no new Go dependency).
- Each response stores one deny event through recordEvent with Reason authorization_required or authorization_unavailable (added to internal/proxy/reasons.go and RecordBlocked), the JAUD-05 pre-swap URL, user_sub, and the OAuth provider in Event.UserTokenProvider (W-P3-PUS-10), never Event.Provider. logDecision gains pending_id. bridgeEvent in internal/alertpipeline returns no finding for these two reasons or user_token_unavailable.
- Counter warden.jit.total{outcome=created|reused|already_granted|cache_hit|cp_unavailable|rate_limited, provider} in internal/observability, provider limited to configured ids else other. No token, status_token or body is logged.
- With no perUser mappings the stage never runs and the allow path gains no allocations or locks.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/connect: add AuthorizationRequired and its HTTP body builder; add docs/schemas/authorization_required.v1.json and a struct-tag schema test.
2. internal/config/remote.go: add RemoteProvider.CreatePending using the shared CP client; map 404 from an older CP to unavailable.
3. internal/proxy/proxy.go: add the PendingCreator interface and SetPendingCreator atomic seam (new); internal/worker/wiring.go sets it when controlPlane.endpoint is set.
4. New internal/proxy/jit.go: pendingCache (LRU, singleflight from golang.org/x/sync, per-key breaker, epoch invalidation) and the jitDeny stage; new writeJSONResponse in internal/proxy/http.go next to writeErrorResponse.
5. internal/proxy/http.go runRequestStages: call jitDeny after swapSecrets; add the two reason constants to reasons.go and the metric to internal/observability.
6. internal/alertpipeline/bridge.go: skip the two JIT reasons and user_token_unavailable in bridgeEvent.
7. Tests: internal/proxy/jit_test.go (zero upstream hits, golden body, CP down, nil creator, user_token_unavailable, cache and singleflight, already granted), a RemoteProvider httptest test, and internal/alertpipeline/bridge_test.go.

### 3/7 · W-P3-JIT-03

**Return JSON-RPC results for MCP calls missing a grant**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#147](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/147)

MCP clients treat a plain 403 as a transport error, so the model never sees the authorize link. When the request is MCP over HTTP, answer a missing grant with a JSON-RPC result or error that carries the same authorization_required object and the original request id. Detection must not depend on the MCP gateway being configured. The stdio wedge is out of scope because it does no secret swap.

**Requirements**

- jitDeny classifies MCP itself: s.wasMCP when set, otherwise protocol.IsMCP(Content-Type, s.reqBody) on the body already read (mcpRequestScan returns early when s.gw is nil). No second body read.
- tools/call with an id: HTTP 200 with JSON-RPC result {isError:true, content:[{type:"text", text: message + " " + authorize_url}], structuredContent: <AuthorizationRequired>}; the id is echoed verbatim (string or number), Mcp-Session-Id is echoed when present, and the text is capped at 1 KiB.
- Other methods with an id: JSON-RPC error -32042 (URL elicitation required) with data {elicitations:[{mode:"url", elicitationId: pending_id, url: authorize_url, message}], warden: <AuthorizationRequired>}. Notifications, batches and legacy HTTP+SSE POSTs get the W-P3-JIT-02 HTTP 403 JSON.
- internal/connect records the MCP protocol revision that the -32042 code comes from as a constant with a test; if the targeted revision has no URL elicitation error, every method with an id gets the tools/call result shape instead.
- Reply with application/json unless Accept excludes it; only then send exactly one `event: message` SSE event with the same JSON and end the response.
- The 503 authorization_unavailable and user_token_unavailable cases use the same result or error shape with that error value.
- Builders MCPToolResult(id, body) and MCPError(id, body) live in internal/connect so W-P4-MGW-07 can reuse them; no file under internal/mcp/stdio changes.
- Events use Protocol mcp, Tool from the gateway verdict when available, and the JIT reasons. The JSON-RPC answer is a deliberate exception to the W-P2-WBND-03 plain-JSON MCP deny rule, noted in code comments and in W-P3-JIT-05.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/connect: add MCPToolResult, MCPError and a small envelope decoder (method, id, batch, notification) reusing the extractID approach from internal/mcp/stdio/pump.go (copied, not imported).
2. internal/proxy/jit.go: add MCP classification and choose HTTP, tool result or error per the rules above.
3. internal/proxy/jit.go: add Accept negotiation and single-event SSE framing.
4. Golden fixtures internal/proxy/testdata/jit/mcp_result.golden.json, mcp_error.golden.json and mcp_sse.golden.txt.
5. Tests in internal/proxy/jit_mcp_test.go and internal/connect/mcp_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given tools/call with id "abc" and no grant, the response is HTTP 200 with result.isError true, result.structuredContent.error == "authorization_required" and id "abc"; numeric id 7 is echoed as 7: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestJITMCPToolResult`.
- [ ] With the MCP gateway unset (gw nil) the same tools/call still gets the JSON-RPC result: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestJITMCPWithoutGateway`.
- [ ] Given Accept: text/event-stream only, internal/mcp/sse.Scan reads exactly one event whose data equals the JSON body.
- [ ] Given tools/list with no grant, error.code is -32042 and error.data.elicitations[0].elicitationId equals pending_id; a notification gets the plain 403 JSON; the upstream sees zero requests in every case.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/connect -run TestMCPBuilders` passes and `git diff --stat main -- internal/mcp/stdio` is empty.

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-JIT-02`](jit-authorization.md#27--w-p3-jit-02) Return structured 403 for HTTP when a grant is missing

### 4/7 · W-P3-JIT-04

**Add /connect/{id}/status long-poll on the CP**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#148](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/148)

Add GET /connect/{id}/status so the agent, the user's portal or a P4 park waiter can wait for a pending to finish and then retry. The agent usually does not hold a Warden user token, so the endpoint accepts the per-pending status_token, a worker credential bound to the pending's agent, or the user's portal session. Waiters are woken through a notifying GrantStore decorator, so the callback and decline call sites do not change. This is control-plane only.

**Requirements**

- GET /connect/{id}/status in internal/oauthbroker, mounted only when consent is configured and listed in the W-P1-SSO-05 authz route table. Response 200 {status: pending|granted|denied|expired, reason, expires_at, expires_in} with Cache-Control: no-store; never sub, email or scopes.
- Auth: Authorization: Bearer <status_token> compared in constant time with the JIT-01 HMAC; a worker credential (WorkerAuthenticator) whose heartbeat agentID equals the pending's agent_id; or a W-P3-CSIG-04 portal session whose (iss, sub) matches the pending. Unknown ids and any other credential get the same 404 body. A token in the query string is ignored.
- wait uses ParseWait in new package internal/longpoll (moved from internal/controlplane/policyserver.go parseWait, same 1s–60s clamp; absent means answer at once). A terminal status returns immediately; each waiter's timer is min(wait, expires_at − now). Status is computed lazily, so expires_at <= now reads expired before the retention ticker runs.
- Waiters wait on the W-P3-BRKR-02 GrantStore Subscribe channel, which closes on CompletePending and on expiry. A thin decorator around GrantStore adds one rule: CompletePending(granted) also marks every active pending for the same (user_key, provider) whose scopes are a subset of the granted scopes as granted, sets completed_at and closes their channels.
- The handler re-reads the row on entry, on every wake, every 5s and on timeout, so a missed wake only delays the answer and multiple CP replicas stay correct.
- Limits: 8 waiters per pending and 2,048 in total, else 429 with Retry-After: 1. Client disconnect frees a waiter at once and the map entry is removed when its last waiter leaves.
- Gauge warden_cp_connect_status_waiters and counter warden_cp_connect_status_total{result=pending|granted|denied|expired|not_found|limited}. One info log per pending state change with pending_id, provider, agent, outcome and duration; no sub at info level, never the status_token.
- Worker callers authenticate only with a worker cert (W-P2-WCA-04 mTLS) whose heartbeat agentID equals the pending's agent_id; a `wwt_` bearer is rejected with 401. Waiter limits stay 8 per pending and 2,048 in total.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/longpoll: ParseWait and the min/max constants; internal/controlplane/policyserver.go calls it instead of its local parseWait.
2. New internal/oauthbroker/waiters.go: waiterHub with limits and cleanup over GrantStore.Subscribe, and matchingStore wrapping CompletePending with the new CompleteMatchingPendings.
3. New internal/oauthbroker/status_http.go: credential resolution (status_token, worker principal, portal session), uniform 404, select over hub channel, timer, 5s re-read ticker and ctx.
4. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go Handler(): wrap the store with matchingStore, mount the route, add the authz table row.
5. Tests in internal/oauthbroker/status_http_test.go and internal/longpoll/longpoll_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a waiter on wait=30s holding the status_token, CompletePending(granted) makes it return granted within 1s: `go test -race ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestStatusLongPoll`.
- [ ] Given two pendings from different agents for the same user and provider, completing one wakes both waiters with granted.
- [ ] Given wait=120s and a fake clock the wait is clamped to 60s and returns pending; when expires_at passes during the wait the response is expired without a ticker run.
- [ ] A wrong status_token, another user's portal session, a worker credential for a different agent and an unknown id each get 404 with identical bodies: `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestStatusAuth`.
- [ ] CompletePending(denied), as the W-P3-PORT-03 decline calls it, wakes a waiter with denied, and after 1,000 waiters are cancelled the waiter map is empty: `go test -race ./internal/oauthbroker -run 'TestStatusDeclineWakes|TestStatusWaiterCleanup'`.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/controlplane` passes with parseWait moved to internal/longpoll.

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-JIT-01`](jit-authorization.md#17--w-p3-jit-01) Add CP endpoint to create or reuse pending authorizations; [`W-P3-CSIG-04`](consent-auth.md#47--w-p3-csig-04) Add the portal session middleware, CSRF, logout and console isolation; [`W-P2-WCA-04`](worker-mtls.md#48--w-p2-wca-04) Accept worker certs in WorkerAuthenticator and add /control/renew; [`W-P1-SSO-05`](console-sso-rbac.md#511--w-p1-sso-05) Enforce role checks on every dashboard route and replace the bearer write guard in oidc mode

### 5/7 · W-P3-JIT-05

**Document the authorization_required contract**

Type **docs** · Size **S** · Issue [#149](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/149)

Add docs/jit-authorization.md so agent and client authors know what a missing grant looks like on each protocol, how to wait for consent and when to retry. The schema and golden fixtures are created by W-P3-JIT-02 and W-P3-JIT-03; this ticket writes the contract around them and a drift test that keeps the examples in the doc equal to the fixtures.

**Requirements**

- Sections for HTTP/1.1 (403 authorization_required, 503 authorization_unavailable and user_token_unavailable), h2 and gRPC (grpc-status 7), MCP over HTTP (tools/call result, -32042 error, notifications and batches, JSON and single-event SSE), and MCP over stdio (the server's own egress gets the HTTP 403).
- Status endpoint: the three accepted credentials, the status_token sent as a Bearer header and never in a URL, wait clamped to 1–60s, statuses, uniform 404, 429 limits and lazy expiry.
- Retry guidance: poll with wait <= 60s; after granted retry the original request once; retry non-idempotent calls only after the user confirms; stop on denied or expired; honour Retry-After on 503; use expires_in rather than local clock math.
- Operator section: consent.publicURL and consent.connect.pendingTTL, allowlisting the consent.publicURL origin for agents that poll (JIT never auto-allows it), the JIT reasons and metrics, and that JIT raises no alerts.
- State that the MCP JSON-RPC answer is a deliberate exception to the W-P2-WBND-03 plain-JSON deny rule, and that body fields are versioned and may only be added.
- Drift test uses only the standard library.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add docs/jit-authorization.md with fenced JSON examples copied from internal/proxy/testdata/jit/.
2. Add new internal/proxy/jit_doc_test.go that extracts the fenced JSON examples and compares them to the golden fixtures.
3. Link the doc from docs/architecture.md and docs/control-plane.md, and reference docs/schemas/authorization_required.v1.json.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestJITDocMatchesGolden` passes and fails when a fixture changes without the doc.
- [ ] The doc has sections for HTTP/1.1, h2/gRPC, MCP over HTTP (JSON and SSE), MCP over stdio, the status endpoint, retry guidance and operator setup.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-JIT-03`](jit-authorization.md#37--w-p3-jit-03) Return JSON-RPC results for MCP calls missing a grant; [`W-P3-JIT-04`](jit-authorization.md#47--w-p3-jit-04) Add /connect/{id}/status long-poll on the CP; [`W-P3-JIT-06`](jit-authorization.md#67--w-p3-jit-06) Return authorization_required on HTTP/2 and gRPC streams

### 6/7 · W-P3-JIT-06

**Return authorization_required on HTTP/2 and gRPC streams**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#301](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/301)

ALPN h2 traffic goes through handleGRPC and serveGRPCStream in internal/proxy/grpc.go, which swap placeholders outside runRequestStages. Run the same JIT logic there so a per-user placeholder without a grant is answered on the stream and never forwarded. This is worker-only and reuses the W-P3-JIT-02 cache and CP client.

**Requirements**

- When per-user resolution in serveGRPCStream reports a grant error (W-P3-PUS-04), call the shared JIT path from internal/proxy/jit.go; non-gRPC h2 requests get the 403 JSON body and headers from W-P3-JIT-02 on the stream.
- application/grpc requests get HTTP 200 with trailers grpc-status 7 (PERMISSION_DENIED) and grpc-message 'authorization_required <authorize_url>', percent-encoded and capped at 1 KiB.
- authorization_unavailable and user_token_unavailable map to 503 JSON on plain h2 and grpc-status 14 (UNAVAILABLE) on gRPC.
- Nothing is sent to the upstream h2 transport for that stream; other streams on the same connection keep working.
- Events and metrics match W-P3-JIT-02 (Protocol grpc or http2, same reasons).

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/connect: add GRPCStatus(body) returning code and message.
2. internal/proxy/grpc.go serveGRPCStream: after per-user resolution, branch to the shared jitDeny helper refactored to write to an http.ResponseWriter.
3. Tests in internal/proxy/grpc_jit_test.go with an h2 client and a fake upstream counting streams.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given an h2 gRPC call with a per-user placeholder and no grant, the client sees grpc-status 7 and the fake upstream counts zero streams: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestJITGRPC`.
- [ ] A non-gRPC h2 request gets the same 403 JSON as HTTP/1.1.
- [ ] A second stream on the same connection to an allowed host still succeeds.
- [ ] With no perUser mappings `go test ./internal/proxy -run GRPC` passes unchanged.

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-JIT-02`](jit-authorization.md#27--w-p3-jit-02) Return structured 403 for HTTP when a grant is missing

### 7/7 · W-P3-JIT-07

**Add end-to-end test for the JIT consent loop**

Type **test** · Size **M** · Issue [#302](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/302)

Prove the feature's done_when in one test: a request missing a grant is denied with a pending, the user consents through the portal, the status long-poll returns granted, and a retry reaches upstream with the user's token. The test runs an in-process CP, worker, fake OAuth provider and fake upstream under the integration build tag. It changes no production code.

**Requirements**

- Build tag integration; in-process CP with consent, broker and portal; worker enrolled with a cert from the W-P2-WCA test CA; a perUser mapping to a fake provider; fake upstream counting requests.
- Covers HTTP 403, MCP tools/call result with the gateway unset, and gRPC status 7.
- Drives consent through /portal/connect/{id}, /connect/start and /connect/callback with a test portal session.
- Asserts the status long-poll (status_token) returns granted within 1s and the single retry reaches upstream with the fake provider's access token.
- Asserts zero upstream requests before the grant, and 503 authorization_unavailable with the CP stopped.
- Asserts no access token or status_token appears in captured logs or stored events.

**Implementation plan**

1. New test/integration/jit_test.go wiring CP, worker, fake provider and fake upstream with httptest.
2. Helpers to create a portal session and follow the consent redirects.
3. Log capture via a test slog handler to check for token leaks.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test -tags integration ./test/integration -run TestJITConsentLoop` passes.
- [ ] The test fails if the upstream sees any request before consent.
- [ ] The test fails if the status long-poll takes more than 1s after the callback.
